ACTION: Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-skills/references/flowcharts.md (SKILL.md requires this before adding a flowchart: when one earns its place, plus the graphviz style rules and render tool).

ACTION: Read skills/cache-invalidation/SKILL.md (the current text, so the flowchart matches its comment density, naming and placement, and doesn't duplicate guidance already there).

ACTION: Read specs/cache-invalidation-baseline.md (the saved reasons from the 11 of 15 wrong-purge runs, so I can classify the failure and key each decision node to a predicate that addresses what the agents said).

I'm reading three files before I write the flowchart, and I haven't edited anything yet.

The flowchart reference comes first because the skill requires it. I also need the current `SKILL.md` and your baseline reasons. The nodes should test things an agent can observe, such as whether a stale read is harmful or whether the key has a TTL. I'd rather take those from the reasons the agents gave for purging than guess them. The reasons will also show whether this is agents breaking a rule they know under pressure, or agents misjudging which option fits. That decides whether the flowchart needs a rationalization table or red flags alongside it.

Once I've read them, I'll add the flowchart to `skills/cache-invalidation/SKILL.md` and send you the exact text. After that I'll re-run the same three scenarios, 5 reps each, with the flowchart in place and compare against the 11 of 15 baseline.
